sections.html: This small freshwater pipefish originates from Western Africa, from Cameroon to Gabon and in the Zaire and Ogowe Rivers. Origin: Cameroon-Gabon, Congo, Angola.
These fish inhabit freshwater as well as brackish water habitats.

This species, and in fact all freshwater pipefish, need a special tank of their own in order to thrive because they are slow eaters. They need regular water changes and a clean tank, but will give their owner much pleasure by displaying beautiful colouration and interesting behaviour.
Addition of sea salt (1-2 teaspoons per 10 litres of water) will increase the vitality of these fish.
They eat only live food like daphnia, cyclops, brine shrimp and the smallest fish fry.

Breeding has been performed successfully in captivity on several occasions. The female lays her eggs onto the breeding pouch of the male. The eggs are attached to the male behind the vent, within an area bordered by 2 folds, which form the breeding pouch.
